strings.title: Let the Abuser Feel the Victim's Pain
strings.hint: Compare the company's exit log with the first statement. Who quoted the note word for word before anyone read it to him?
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: Fahad Sultan Al-Anazi — the former fiancé.

Fahad could not accept the broken engagement and saw himself as the 'humiliated victim.' He watched Reem for two weeks using a dark car and a temporary phone number, then entered her apartment with the spare key he had kept from their engagement. During a brief confrontation, the vase broke and her wristwatch stopped at 20:26. He left the note 'Let the abuser feel the victim's pain.' to reverse their roles and portray himself as the wronged party.

The evidence against him: the partial fingerprint on the vase, the cells under her fingernails, the company exit log showing 19:20 rather than the time he claimed, the entrance footage at 20:32, and his knowledge of the note's wording before it was shown to him.
strings.summary.text: On the morning of 16 July 2024, police received a report that a woman had been killed in her apartment after contact with her stopped the previous evening. The victim was found dead in the living room, with clear signs of violence. There was no damage to the doors or windows, suggesting that she knew the offender and let them in — or that they had a key.
strings.summary.victim.name: Reem Khalid Al-Otaibi
strings.scene.intro: An orderly apartment suggests a quiet life interrupted by a brief confrontation in the living room: a shattered vase beside the sofa, a stained pillow in the bedroom, and a door with no sign of forced entry. The visitor was known to the victim… or had a key.
strings.scene.notes[0]: No damage to doors or windows
strings.scene.notes[1]: Living-room furniture displaced; signs of a struggle beside the sofa
strings.scene.notes[2]: Two tea cups in the sink, one with a lip mark
strings.scene.notes[3]: The spare-key box behind the door is empty
strings.scene.notes[4]: A paper note with a strange message on the living-room table
strings.evidence[0].title: Kitchen knife
strings.evidence[0].desc: The likely murder weapon, from the victim's own kitchen set. Dried blood remains on the blade, and the handle was partly wiped with a cloth.
strings.evidence[1].title: Broken vase
strings.evidence[1].desc: Shattered during the struggle. A partial fingerprint on the base does not belong to the victim; the preliminary match to one suspect is 87%.
strings.evidence[2].title: Mobile phone
strings.evidence[2].desc: The screen is cracked. Last activity: an unsent message at 20:11 reading 'If you get this, I'm scared.' Sent to the digital laboratory.
strings.evidence[3].title: Bloodstains on a pillow
strings.evidence[3].desc: A transfer pattern rather than direct bleeding. The offender probably touched the pillow after the attack, suggesting a personal relationship.
strings.evidence[4].title: The paper note
strings.evidence[4].desc: A sheet bearing the slanted handwritten words: 'Let the abuser feel the victim's pain.' No usable fingerprints were found.
strings.evidence[5].title: Two tea cups
strings.evidence[5].desc: Two hastily washed cups, one retaining a lip mark. The victim had received a visitor shortly before the crime.
strings.evidence[6].title: The missing spare key
strings.evidence[6].desc: The key box behind the door is empty. The neighbor confirms that Reem usually kept a spare key there.
strings.evidence[7].title: Gray fabric fibers
strings.evidence[7].desc: A cotton and synthetic blend consistent with a man's gray jacket. No matching garment was found in the apartment.
strings.evidence[8].title: Missed-call log
strings.evidence[8].desc: 23 missed calls from the same temporary number over the past two weeks, the last on the night of the crime.
strings.evidence[9].title: Torn rubber glove
strings.evidence[9].desc: Sweat inside is partially suitable for DNA comparison. The offender probably tried to clean the scene.
strings.evidence[10].title: Victim's wristwatch
strings.evidence[10].desc: Stopped at 20:26 when its glass broke during the struggle — the almost certain time of the crime.
strings.evidence[11].title: Sports-shoe print
strings.evidence[11].desc: Size 43 with a common tread pattern, pointing toward the exit.
strings.suspects[0].name: Abdullah Nasser Al-Harbi
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'I was in my apartment watching a match until midnight. I heard a brief commotion and thought it was just an argument.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: I only know Reem as a neighbor. We had an old dispute over parking that led to complaints from both sides, but things settled down. On the evening of the crime I heard glass breaking at about twenty past eight, followed by complete silence. I didn't open my door because I'm used to arguments in the building. I saw no one on the stairs, and I'm willing to hand over my phone to prove I never left my apartment.
strings.suspects[1].name: Fahad Sultan Al-Anazi
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I was at work until nine in the evening, then went straight home.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: Reem ended our relationship two months ago. I accepted it, however painful it was. I haven't visited her apartment since the breakup, and I know nothing about a spare key. Whoever wrote 'Let the abuser feel the victim's pain.' clearly wants to frame me. I was the one humiliated in that relationship, and everyone knows she was the one who wronged me.
strings.suspects[2].name: Saud Mutlaq Al-Shammari
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'I was making my usual rounds between the buildings from eight until quarter to nine.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: I've worked here for eleven years and there has never been a single murder. Yes, there's a gap in the camera recording. I admit I disabled it myself because I left my post on personal business and was afraid of a complaint and dismissal. I saw a dark car parked away from the building twice this week, but couldn't make out the driver. I told the investigator that on the first day.
strings.suspects[3].name: Noura Abdulrahman Al-Qahtani
strings.suspects[3].alibi: 'I was at a family dinner, documented in photos, until half past ten.'
strings.suspects[3].statement: Reem was my friend before she was my business partner. Our financial dispute over the restaurant project's payment of 18,000 was being resolved. She transferred half to me a week ago. I called at 20:15, but she didn't answer, so I assumed she was asleep. You should investigate whoever was watching her. She told me herself about a car that had been following her for two weeks.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Umm Mohammed
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I noticed the apartment door had been ajar since dawn. At nine I knocked, but she didn't answer. I pushed the door slightly, saw the scene and called the police immediately. Reem was quiet and well liked, but she had seemed frightened lately. A week ago she asked me whether the building's camera actually worked.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Khalid
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I delivered an order to Apartment 21, then took the elevator down. At the entrance, a man in a dark cap and gray jacket bumped into me. He was walking fast with his head lowered and didn't even apologize. He was taller than average, had an athletic build, and wore strong cologne.
strings.witnesses[1].items[0].label: Entrance camera still — 20:32
strings.witnesses[2].name: Abu Faisal
strings.witnesses[2].statement: I heard glass breaking around 20:20, followed by a brief muffled scream and then total silence. I thought it was a loud television. A few minutes later I heard a door being closed unusually quietly. Who closes a door so carefully after a fight?
strings.witnesses[3].name: Hind
strings.witnesses[3].statement: Reem was afraid of someone she said 'couldn't accept that it was over.' Two days before the crime she showed me a threatening message from an unfamiliar number, then deleted it out of fear. I called her at 20:15, but she didn't answer, and my messages remained unread.
strings.witnesses[3].items[0].label: The threat as Hind remembers it
strings.witnesses[3].items[0].text: 'You will know how it feels to be humiliated. No one but you will understand what it means.'
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: First incident report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body:
Transcript of the call to the operations room:
The caller, neighbor Umm Mohammed, reports that Apartment 34's door has been ajar since morning, with an unusual smell coming from inside. She last saw the victim yesterday afternoon.
The nearest patrol was dispatched immediately and the forensics team notified.
strings.folders[0].docs[1].title: Second incident report
strings.folders[0].docs[1].body:
An earlier complaint by the victim, Reem Al-Otaibi, against an unknown person:
She felt watched outside the building and repeatedly noticed a dark car in the parking spaces opposite.
The report was closed for insufficient evidence, with a recommendation for increased patrols. That recommendation was not implemented.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Autopsy report (Jessica)
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body:
Autopsy summary — Dr. Jessica Karam:
Death resulted from two penetrating chest wounds made by a sharp kitchen blade. Estimated time of death: between 20:00 and 21:00 on 15 July.
Defensive bruising on the forearms. Blood transfer on a bedroom pillow is inconsistent with direct bleeding.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Toxicology report (Arsene)
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body:
Toxicology report — Dr. Arsene Nasri:
No traces of drugs or poison in the blood.
Foreign skin cells under the right-hand fingernails were sent for DNA comparison. Results are in the confidential files.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Fingerprint examination
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body:
A partial fingerprint on the broken vase's base does not belong to the victim.
Preliminary match to suspect Fahad Al-Anazi's sample: 87%.
The other fingerprints recovered from the living room belong to the victim and her neighbor.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: DNA analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body:
DNA from the cells recovered beneath the victim's fingernails belongs to a male.
Comparison with the suspects' samples is ongoing. The final result is in the confidential files.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Knife examination
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body:
The knife belongs to the victim's own kitchen set.
Its handle was partly wiped with a cloth, leaving gray fibers matching the sample recovered from the table edge.
strings.folders[2].docs[3].title: Bloodstain pattern report
strings.folders[2].docs[3].body:
The stains in the living room indicate a brief struggle beside the sofa.
The pillow stain is a transfer pattern, suggesting the offender touched it after the attack. This personal behavior suggests a prior relationship with the victim.
strings.folders[3].name: Laboratory analyses
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Gray-fiber analysis
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body:
The fibers are a cotton and synthetic blend consistent with a man's gray jacket.
No matching garment was found in the victim's apartment.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Glove-residue analysis
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body:
The torn rubber glove recovered from the kitchen bin has sweat residue inside.
The sample is partially suitable for DNA comparison.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Handwriting analysis
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body:
The note's phrase ('Let the abuser feel the victim's pain.') was written with a slant and heavy pen pressure, indicating tension.
The slant and joined strokes resemble suspect Fahad Al-Anazi's handwriting sample to a moderate-to-high degree.
strings.folders[4].name: Interviews
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Interview: Abdullah Al-Harbi
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body:
Confirmed hearing a commotion around 20:20 and said he never left his apartment.
Admitted an old parking dispute with the victim and mutual nuisance complaints.
No witnesses confirm that he remained in the apartment.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Interview: Fahad Al-Anazi (first)
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body:
Said he had not visited the victim since their engagement ended two months ago, and that he left work at 21:00.
Requested a lawyer as soon as he was asked about the spare key.
strings.folders[4].docs[2].title: Interview: Fahad Al-Anazi (second)
strings.folders[4].docs[2].body:
Confronted with the company's exit log (19:20), he changed his account and claimed he had driven around alone.
He denied knowing about the paper note, then quoted it word for word before it was read to him. This key point was recorded in the interview.
strings.folders[4].docs[3].title: Interview: Saud Al-Shammari
strings.folders[4].docs[3].body:
Struggled to explain the gap in the camera recordings (20:05–20:45).
Later admitted leaving his post on personal business and disabling the recording to avoid disciplinary action.
strings.folders[4].docs[4].title: Interview: Noura Al-Qahtani
strings.folders[4].docs[4].body:
Admitted a financial dispute over a project payment of 18,000 and an argument over the phone three days earlier.
Provided evidence that she attended a family dinner until 22:30.
strings.folders[4].docs[5].title: Interview: Khalid (delivery worker)
strings.folders[4].docs[5].body:
Described a man in a dark cap and gray jacket who bumped into him at the entrance at 20:32 while concealing his face.
Recognized the man's build from the suspects' photographs with reasonable confidence.
strings.folders[5].name: Records
strings.folders[5].docs[0].title: Victim's call log
strings.folders[5].docs[0].body:
23 missed calls from one number over the past two weeks, the last at 20:11 on the night of the crime.
The number belongs to a temporary SIM card. Its point of sale is being traced.
strings.folders[5].docs[1].title: Tech Data access log
strings.folders[5].docs[1].body:
The Tech Data company gate records show employee Fahad Al-Anazi leaving at 19:20, not 21:00 as he claimed.
There is no record of his returning that night.
strings.folders[5].docs[2].title: Police attendance report
strings.folders[5].docs[2].body:
The patrol arrived at 09:30. The door was ajar, with no damage; the victim was in the living room. The scene suggested a brief struggle.
The site was secured and forensic investigators and medical examiners were called.
strings.folders[5].docs[3].title: Surveillance camera report
strings.folders[5].docs[3].body:
The entrance camera recorded a man in a cap leaving at 20:32.
The guard-booth camera has a 40-minute gap (20:05–20:45).
There are no cameras on the rear staircase.
strings.folders[5].docs[4].title: Building visitor log
strings.folders[5].docs[4].body:
The guard's ledger records no visitors to Apartment 34 on the day of the crime.
The last recorded visit was 9 days earlier, with the incomplete initials: F. A.
strings.folders[6].name: Court orders
strings.folders[6].docs[0].title: Apartment search warrant
strings.folders[6].docs[0].body: A court warrant authorizing a search of the crime scene, collection of evidence and securing of the contents of Apartment 34.
strings.folders[6].docs[1].title: Phone-data extraction warrant
strings.folders[6].docs[1].body: Authorization to extract call records and deleted messages from the victim's phone and trace the temporary number.
strings.folders[6].docs[2].title: Arrest warrant
strings.folders[6].docs[2].body: An arrest warrant for the principal suspect following the fingerprint findings, exit log and handwriting comparison.
strings.folders[7].name: Recorded statements
strings.folders[7].docs[0].title: Abdullah's denial
strings.folders[7].docs[0].body: Denied any involvement, maintained his account and offered to hand over his phone voluntarily.
strings.folders[7].docs[1].title: Fahad's denial
strings.folders[7].docs[1].body: Denied involvement despite being confronted with the exit log. On his lawyer's advice, remained silent after the question about the note.
strings.folders[7].docs[2].title: Saud's admission about the camera
strings.folders[7].docs[2].body: Admitted disabling the recording for 40 minutes while away from his post, but denied involvement in the crime. Referred for disciplinary review.
strings.folders[7].docs[3].title: Final confrontation record
strings.folders[7].docs[3].body:
The principal suspect was confronted with the combined evidence: the fingerprint, cells, records and handwriting.
He remained completely silent in his lawyer's presence.
strings.folders[8].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[8].docs[0].title: Messages recovered from the phone
strings.folders[8].docs[0].body:
The digital laboratory recovered deleted messages from the temporary number:
'You will know how it feels to be humiliated.' — 'No one but you will understand what it means.' — 'I'll give this the ending your actions deserve.'
The phrasing matches suspect Fahad Al-Anazi's writing sample.
strings.folders[8].docs[1].title: Final comparison report
strings.folders[8].docs[1].body:
DNA comparison is complete. The sample from beneath the fingernails matches suspect Fahad Al-Anazi, with an error probability of 1 in 5.8 billion.
The case is ready for referral.
strings.reports[0].title: Investigator's preliminary report
strings.reports[0].author: Captain M. Al-Dhaheri — lead investigator
strings.reports[0].body:
The lack of forced entry suggests the victim let the offender in, or they used a key.
The commotion at 20:20 is consistent with the watch stopping at 20:26 and the man in the cap leaving at 20:32.
Lines of inquiry: personal relationships, the temporary number and the gap in the guard's camera recording.
strings.reports[1].title: Crime-scene examination
strings.reports[1].author: Forensics Department
strings.reports[1].body:
Examination shows a brief struggle in the living room, with the offender entering the bedroom after the attack.
12 items of evidence were collected, chiefly the knife, vase, paper note and fabric fibers.
strings.reports[2].title: Phone examination report
strings.reports[2].author: Digital laboratory
strings.reports[2].body:
An unsent message at 20:11 reads: 'If you get this, I'm scared.'
Conversations with the temporary number were deliberately deleted one day before the crime. Recovery is ongoing; results are in the confidential files.
strings.notes[0].text: Remember: check the reports and communications
strings.notes[1].text: Compare Fahad's exit time with his first statement
strings.notes[2].text: Where did the spare key go? Ask the neighbor
